settings.title: SHIKISHA-TERM Settings
settings.tabbar_width.hint: Leave empty to fit the tab names

settings.workspace.name: Name

settings.back.confirm: There are unsaved changes. Discard them and go back?
settings.browser.ask.text.ph: Press this when you have finished reading
settings.browser.ask.label: Button

tui.ask.label: Done

settings.ws.save_first: Save first. Export and import both work on the settings as stored on disk
settings.ws.imported.moved: Those places were taken, so the scripts went elsewhere: {moved}
settings.ws.export.title: Where to write the workspace
settings.ws.import.title: Workspace file to import
settings.tab.name: Display name
settings.tab.id.hint: Set this and you can rename the tab without breaking automation
settings.tab.cwd.hint: The AI looks at the project here
settings.tab.profile.hint: Rule used to detect the state. Use it for an AI running over SSH
settings.browser.url.hint: Opened on start; automation can navigate from there
settings.browser.url.bad: Use an http:// or https:// address — others cannot be opened
settings.container.name: Container
settings.container.hint: The folder inside the container/WSL is set here
settings.template.hint: Starting from a template is easier
settings.restart_note: Tabs whose connection, encoding or scrollback changed are marked with ⟳. They switch over when you press Ctrl+B r in the app, so your running work is not cut off.
settings.phone.enable.label: Let me check status and send instructions from my phone
settings.phone.only_while_running: Reachable only while the app is running
settings.pick.title: Choose
settings.phone.lan: Tailscale not found. Your home network ({ip}) can be used
settings.phone.scan: Scan this with your phone camera
settings.phone.note: Only people on the same network can connect. Installing Tailscale (free) means only your own devices can reach it, even from outside — this is the safest option. Without Tailscale it works on your home network only (anyone on the same Wi-Fi who knows the URL and token could operate it). It is never published to the internet unless you write that in the config file yourself.

automation.editor.code.ph: Write what should happen. Leave it empty to do nothing
automation.editor.ask: Ask an AI to write it

automation.editor.no_ai: Install Claude Code, Codex CLI or Gemini CLI to describe this in your own words.
automation.editor.saved_new: Automation saved. Press Save as well
automation.editor.check: Check the result and press Apply
automation.on_load.hint: Save the HTML, hand it to an AI (fires on every navigation)
automation.on_press: When the human presses the banner
automation.on_press.hint: Only while a script has put the banner up with browser_ask (waiting for a sign-in, say)
automation.on_start.hint: e.g. move to the working folder and resume the previous session
automation.on_done.hint: e.g. hand the result to another tab, or notify you
automation.on_question.hint: Return a string to answer automatically, or nothing to leave it to a human
automation.on_busy.hint: e.g. check on it periodically while it works (advanced)
help.page.title: How to write automation
remote.err.no_network: No reachable network was found. To use this from outside you need a private network such as Tailscale, or to be on the same local network
remote.err.lan_only: Tailscale was not found, so your home network is used. Anyone on it who has the token can operate this
remote.err.public: {ip} is reachable from outside. If you really need this, set remote.allow_public to true (note that this lets anyone with the token run commands through your AI)
remote.err.start: Could not start the phone feature ({addr}): {error}
remote.err.in_use: {addr} is already taken by another process. Check whether an earlier SHIKISHA-TERM is still running
msg.nav.bad_url: Cannot go there: {url} (only http:// and https:// pages open here)
msg.press_nowhere: >> The banner on "{name}" was pressed, but nothing is written in on_press (the settings screen has a slot for it)
msg.press_auto_off: >> Automation is off, so the banner button does nothing (Ctrl+B a turns it back on)
ai.prompt:
You are a converter that writes automation scripts for SHIKISHA-TERM.
Write the contents of `{event}.lua` so that it does the following.

## Output rules (strict)
- Always start with <<<LUA and end with >>>; write only Lua code in between
- No greetings, explanations, confirmations, questions or code fences
- Do not wrap it in function ... end (write only the body)
- Do not use functions or libraries that are absent from the specification
- No need to look up or check files; finish from these instructions alone

## What is wanted
{want}

{layout}
## Specification
{manual}

Now begin with <<<LUA.
ai.tabs.header:
## Tab layout
Name the destination tab (e.g. shikisha.send_to_tab("Review", ...)).
Numbers change when tabs are reordered, so names are safer.
ai.tabs.self: ← the tab this script runs in (tab)
ai.err.no_code: The AI did not return code. Try rephrasing it (reply: {reply})
